fullPassage:
Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are useless and unpleasant places, but actually they are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide numerous benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season of July and August, and it supplies adequate water to local farmers during droughts. Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.

The Camargue / France
The Camargue is a region in southern France where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have spent thousands of years living in the unique environment of the Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They have become powerful and strong as a result of surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick grasses, and weeds are available. If you have ever seen a magnificent image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses from this area.

The Everglades / USA
The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.

What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they are found living together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.

The Sudd / South Sudan
The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, nomadic people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands to feed their herds like sheep, cows, and goats and catch the abundant fish. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically protected the people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River. Nero, the emperor of the Roman empire, sent the military to explore the White Nile in 61 AD, but his soldiers were unable to proceed beyond the Sudd.

Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.

questions.passage: Did you know that February 2nd is World Wetlands Day? Some may wonder whether wetlands are important enough to celebrate every year. They may think wetlands are (A)[useless / valuable] and unpleasant places, but actually they are (B)[unique / ordinary] ecosystems that must be protected because they provide (C)[numerous / limited] benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of threatened and endangered species.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 습지가 쓸모없는(useless) 곳이라고 생각할 수 있지만, 실제로는 독특한(unique) 생태계이며 수많은(numerous) 혜택을 제공한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① useless — unique — numerous: 원문 그대로. 'but actually'로 역접 → (A)는 부정적 단어.
❌ ② valuable(가치 있는): 역접 앞에서 부정적으로 본다는 문맥에 반대.
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): 'must be protected' → 특별한(unique) 생태계.
❌ ④ limited(제한된): 보호 이유가 '많은 혜택'이므로 numerous가 적절.
det.tip: useless ↔ valuable, unique ↔ ordinary, numerous ↔ limited

questions.passage: It functions as a natural sponge, (A)[absorbing / repelling] and gradually releasing surface water such as rain, groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also an (B)[excellent / mediocre] place to observe more than 400 species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The (C)[exotic / common] pink flamingo is one of the most famous species found there.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 카마르그는 물을 흡수하는(absorbing) 스펀지 역할을 하며, 훌륭한(excellent) 조류 관찰지이고, 이국적인(exotic) 홍학이 유명하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② absorbing — excellent — exotic: 원문 그대로.
❌ ① repelling(밀어내는): 스펀지는 물을 흡수하므로 부적절.
❌ ③ mediocre(평범한): '400종 이상' 관찰 가능한 곳은 훌륭한 곳.
❌ ④ common(흔한): '가장 유명한 종' 중 하나이므로 exotic이 적절.
det.tip: absorbing(흡수하는) ↔ repelling(밀어내는), excellent ↔ mediocre, exotic(이국적인) ↔ common(흔한)

questions.passage: Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the (A)[migration / settlement] and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has (B)[flourished / declined] in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017. What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators (C)[coexist / compete].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 이주(migration) 시기에 의존, 플로리다 표범이 번성(flourished), 악어와 앨리게이터가 공존(coexist)한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ migration — flourished — coexist: 원문 그대로.
❌ ① declined(감소했다): 12→230으로 회복했으므로 flourished가 맞음.
❌ ② settlement(정착): 새들의 이동 시기이므로 migration.
❌ ③ compete(경쟁하다): 원문은 공존(coexist).
det.tip: migration(이주) ↔ settlement(정착), flourished(번성하다) ↔ declined(감소하다), coexist(공존하다) ↔ compete(경쟁하다)

questions.passage: Upo is Korea's largest ①<u>untouched</u> wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a ②<u>habitat</u> for a number of threatened and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly ③<u>extinct</u>. Furthermore, Upo prevents floods by absorbing water during the rainy season, and it supplies ④<u>inadequate</u> water to local farmers during droughts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ inadequate(불충분한) → adequate(충분한): 가뭄 시 농부들에게 물을 공급하므로 '충분한'이 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① untouched(손대지 않은): 한국 최대 '자연 그대로의' 습지 — 원문 일치.
✅ ② habitat(서식지): 멸종위기종의 '서식지' — 원문 일치.
✅ ③ extinct(멸종된): 따오기가 '거의 멸종된' 새 — 원문 일치.
❌ ④ inadequate(불충분한) → adequate(충분한): 가뭄 시 물을 '공급'한다는 맥락. ←정답
det.tip: adequate(충분한) ↔ inadequate(불충분한)

questions.passage: The Camargue is also an excellent place to observe more than 400 species of birds. The Camargue is an ①<u>ideal</u> place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off. The area is also known historically for its white horses. The Camargue horses are a special breed, said to be one of the world's oldest, and they have ②<u>spent</u> thousands of years living in the unique environment. They have become powerful and ③<u>weak</u> as a result of surviving in the Camargue. If you have ever seen a ④<u>magnificent</u> image of horses running through water, it is very likely that they are Camargue horses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ weak(약한) → strong(강한): 혹독한 환경에서 생존한 결과 '강해졌다'가 적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ideal(이상적인): 조류 관찰에 이상적인 장소 — 원문 일치.
✅ ② spent(보냈다): 수천 년을 보냈다 — 원문 일치.
❌ ③ weak(약한) → strong(강한): 생존의 결과로 '강해졌다'. ←정답
✅ ④ magnificent(웅장한): 물 속을 달리는 웅장한 이미지 — 원문 일치.
det.tip: powerful and strong(강력하고 강한) ↔ powerful and weak(강력하고 약한): 문맥상 부자연스러운 조합.

questions.passage: The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, ①<u>sustained</u> by the flow of the White Nile. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. The name "Sudd" comes from an Arabic word for "barriers," and the wetland historically ②<u>protected</u> the people from invaders. The Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans spent centuries searching for the starting point of the Nile River. Nero sent the military to explore the White Nile, but his soldiers were ③<u>able</u> to proceed beyond the Sudd. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under ④<u>threat</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ able(할 수 있는) → unable(할 수 없는): 병사들이 수드를 넘어 진행할 수 '없었다'.
det.analysis:
✅ ① sustained(유지되는): 백나일 강에 의해 유지된다 — 원문 일치.
✅ ② protected(보호했다): 침입자로부터 보호했다 — 원문 일치.
❌ ③ able(할 수 있는) → unable(할 수 없는): 장벽(barriers) 역할 → 통과 불가. ←정답
✅ ④ threat(위협): 습지가 위협받고 있다 — 원문 일치.
det.tip: able ↔ unable: 수드가 장벽 역할을 했으므로 병사들이 통과할 수 없었다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② habitat(서식지): 멸종위기종이 사는 곳 — 원문 일치.
❌ ① barrier(장벽): 서식 공간이 아닌 차단물.
❌ ③ shelter(은신처): 유사하지만 생태계 전체를 나타내는 habitat이 정확.
❌ ④ resource(자원): 동물이 사는 '곳'을 뜻하지 않음.
det.tip: habitat = 동식물의 서식지. a habitat for ~ = ~의 서식지.

questions.passage:
________Like Upo, there are other wetlands in the world that help the environment and humans around them. Let's take a look at some of them.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① sponge(스펀지): 물을 흡수하고 서서히 방출 — 스펀지 비유 정확.
❌ ② filter(여과기): 걸러내는 기능이지 흡수/방출이 아님.
❌ ③ dam(댐): 물을 막는 구조물이지 흡수하는 것이 아님.
❌ ④ reservoir(저수지): 저장만 하지 흡수/방출 패턴이 아님.
det.tip: natural sponge = 물을 흡수했다가 서서히 방출하는 자연의 스펀지.

questions.passage: Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has __________ in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population had recovered to about 230 by 2017.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ flourished(번성했다): 12마리에서 230마리로 회복 — 번성.
❌ ① disappeared(사라졌다): 회복 맥락에 반대.
❌ ② struggled(고군분투했다): 결과적으로 회복했으므로 번성이 적절.
❌ ③ declined(감소했다): 230으로 회복된 사실에 반대.
det.tip: flourish = 번성하다, 잘 자라다. 12→230 회복 = flourished.

questions.passage: Wetlands are unique ecosystems that must be protected because they provide <u>numerous</u> benefits to both the environment and humans. For example, Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 numerous와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ many(많은): numerous의 동의어.
❌ ① rare(드문): 반대 의미.
❌ ② limited(제한된): 반대 의미.
❌ ④ essential(필수적인): '중요한'이지 '많은'이 아님.
det.tip: numerous = many = a lot of = a great number of

questions.passage: The Sudd wetland is the largest wetland in Africa, sustained by the flow of the White Nile from Lake Victoria in Uganda. In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. For example, during the dry season, <u>nomadic</u> people move deeper into the wetland and build seasonal homes on naturally occurring islands.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 nomadic과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② wandering(떠돌아다니는): 계절에 따라 이동하는 유목민.
❌ ① permanent(영구적인): 반대 — 유목민은 정착하지 않음.
❌ ③ agricultural(농업의): 목축(herding)과 다른 개념.
❌ ④ coastal(해안의): 지리적 위치이지 생활방식이 아님.
det.tip: nomadic = 유목하는. nomadic people = 유목민. ↔ sedentary(정착하는)

questions.passage: Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue, for example, is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half of the historic Everglades remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills from oil extraction activities. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide <u>valuable</u> benefits to animals, plants, and humans.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 valuable과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① precious(귀중한): valuable의 동의어.
❌ ② minimal(최소한의): 가치와 반대.
❌ ③ temporary(일시적인): 시간 관련이지 가치가 아님.
❌ ④ ordinary(평범한): 특별한 가치와 반대.
det.tip: valuable = precious = invaluable = priceless (귀중한)

questions.passage: Upo is Korea's largest untouched wetland, covering an area as big as 210 soccer fields. First of all, Upo is a habitat for a number of <u>threatened</u> and endangered species. To name a few, there is the rare gasiyeon and the ttaogi, a bird which is nearly extinct.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 threatened와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ secure(안전한): 위협받는 것의 반대.
❌ ① endangered(멸종위기의): threatened와 유사어.
❌ ② harmed(해를 입은): threatened와 유사어.
❌ ③ vulnerable(취약한): threatened와 유사어.
det.tip: threatened(위협받는) ↔ secure(안전한), safe(안전한)

questions.passage: It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands in <u>maintaining</u> our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 maintaining과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② neglecting(방치하는): 유지하는 것의 반대 — 돌보지 않는 것.
❌ ① preserving(보존하는): maintaining과 유사어.
❌ ③ sustaining(지속시키는): maintaining과 유사어.
❌ ④ supporting(지원하는): maintaining과 유사어.
det.tip: maintain(유지하다) ↔ neglect(방치하다), abandon(포기하다)

questions.passage:
(A) It functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and gradually <u>releasing</u> surface water.

(B) The movie studio is <u>releasing</u> a new film next month.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 releasing의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 방출하는 — (B) 공개하는: (A)는 물을 방출, (B)는 영화를 개봉/공개.
❌ ① (A)와 (B)가 뒤바뀜.
❌ ② (A) 해방하는: 물의 방출이지 구속에서의 해방이 아님.
❌ ④ 두 의미 모두 부정확.
det.tip: release: 1) 방출하다(물/가스) 2) 공개/개봉하다(영화/음반) 3) 해방하다(사람)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism"

det.analysis:
✅ ④ habitat(서식지): 동식물이 사는 자연 환경.
❌ ① ecosystem(생태계): 생물과 환경의 상호작용 체계 전체.
❌ ② species(종): 생물 분류 단위.
❌ ③ migration(이주): 계절적 이동.
det.tip: habitat = 서식지. natural habitat = 자연 서식지.

questions.passage: The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the __________ (migrate) and breeding seasons.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.analysis: ✅ migration: 'during the ___ and breeding seasons' — the + 명사 자리. 동사 migrate → 명사 migration.
det.tip: migrate(v) → migration(n) → migratory(adj)

questions.passage: Now that we understand the __________ (important) of wetlands in maintaining our ecosystems, we should consider ways to live without destroying the wetlands that provide valuable benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.analysis: ✅ importance: 'the ___ of wetlands' — the + 명사 + of 구조. 형용사 important → 명사 importance.
det.tip: important(adj) → importance(n). the importance of ~ = ~의 중요성

questions.passage:
The Everglades / USA
The Everglades is a wetland that stretches from Lake Okeechobee to Florida Bay. It functions as a "biological supermarket." Many birds and mammal species rely on the Everglades for food, water, and shelter, particularly during the migration and breeding seasons. For example, the Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults estimated in the wild. But the whole population in the Everglades National Park had recovered to about 230 by 2017.

What is more, the Everglades is the only place where American crocodiles and American alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water, whereas alligators live in ________. However, they are found living together where fresh water from Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water to people in Florida, with one out of every three people relying on the Everglades for drinking water. Unless the Everglades is preserved, millions of people will suffer from a shortage of drinking water.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ fresh water(담수): salt water와 대비되는 환경 — 원문 일치.
❌ ① warm water(따뜻한 물): 온도 기준이 아닌 염도 기준.
❌ ② deep water(깊은 물): 깊이 기준이 아님.
❌ ④ still water(고인 물): 흐름 기준이 아님.
det.tip: salt water(염수/해수) ↔ fresh water(담수/민물)

questions.passage: Wetlands, no matter where they are found, clearly provide habitats for a variety of endangered plant and animal species, as well as humans. Unfortunately, wetlands are currently under threat. The Camargue is decreasing as sea levels rise due to climate change. The Everglades used to be much larger, but due to agriculture and urban development, less than half remains today. The Sudd has been contaminated by oil spills. It is estimated that 64% of the world's wetlands have disappeared. Now that we understand the importance of wetlands, we should consider ways to live __________ that provide valuable benefits to animals, plants, and humans.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 습지를 파괴하지 않으면서(without destroying the wetlands) 사는 방법을 고려해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① without destroying the wetlands: 습지 보존 주제와 일치 — 원문 그대로.
❌ ② by expanding agricultural land(농지 확장): 습지 축소 원인.
❌ ③ while prioritizing urban growth(도시 성장 우선): 습지 축소 원인.
❌ ④ by relocating endangered species(멸종위기종 이주): 습지 보존과 무관.
det.tip: without + V-ing = ~하지 않으면서. 글의 결론부 = 보존 촉구.
